At the 2026 Breakpoint event, Brennan Watt, CEO of Anza, gave a walkthrough of Solana’s wins this year, while sharing what is in store for 2027.

According to Watt, 2026 was a major year for Solana as it migrated its consensus to Alpenglow, slashed the block times in half from 400 ms to 200 ms while doubling capacity.

Recent findings suggest that the Alpenglow upgrade went live on mainnet on October 21, 2026, cutting transaction finality from about 12.8 seconds down to roughly 150 milliseconds. It replaced TowerBFT with Votor, a faster path to reaching agreement.

After Alpenglow, @bw_solana laid out @anza_xyz roadmap for Solana in 2027 Performance: network compute capacity doubles, transactions cut 80% CU units for token accounts Expressivity: vector processing for models running fully onchain, 64 → 96 accounts per transaction, read account data instead of copying it so less data moves per transaction Market Structure: Alpenglow. Next with faster block distribution and Constellation for clearer ordering rules and more competition among validators Resilience: simpler protocol with fewer special cases, safer to change https://t.co/EpvDdSyjln.

Sources indicate that solana recently transitioned to 1.0, marking the network’s graduation from “mainnet beta” to “mainnet” and retiring the beta designation it has carried since launch. Solana 1.0 recognizes the progress on network performance, resilience, and developer experience.

Sources indicate that according to Watt, Solana is eyeing significant improvements in 2027 across four categories. First is Resilience, which involves simplifying the protocol, reducing special cases, and making it safer to change.

“So, we're going to go ahead and simplify the protocol, replacing legacy abstractions and interfaces, pushing more of the execution on chain, and modernizing some of the wire formats. And all of this, you know, enhances resiliency, but it also allows us to move quicker and be more agile and deploy things and evolve the protocol more promptly,” Watt stated.

Second is Market Structure, which centers on Alpenglow, which aims for faster block distribution, and Constellation, which aims for clearer ordering rules and more competition among validators.

According to recent reports, “Several important Alpenglow extensions are coming,” Watt stated. Alpenglow rolls out in two phases: first is Votor, its voting protocol, which is already live on the platform; second is Rotor, a single relay layer planned for a later release that will replace Turbine, the protocol that spreads a block’s data across the network.

Third is Performance, where network compute capacity doubles and transactions use 80% fewer compute units for token accounts. Last is Expressivity, which involves vector processing for models running fully onchain and an increase from 64 to 96 accounts per transaction.

According to recent reports, watt also spoke about improvements in onchain development: “The cost of storing data on Solana came down by 27% this year. And just in the coming two weeks, we're going to bring this thing down by another 7x.”.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

While it’s easy to get starstruck when working for an athlete or other high-profile client, Yohann Sangaré, an agent with eXp’s sports and entertainment division, discourages it. “You come as a problem solver, not a fan,” he said.

Sangaré, a French former professional basketball player who played for 16 years across Europe, sometimes avoids reading up too much about his athlete clients’ accomplishments in their prospective sports so that he can focus on the task at hand: Finding them the right home and advising them on large investments.

Industry observers note that sangaré came to the U.S. when he was hired to work for Tony Parker, his former teammate, in San Antonio, Texas; he started as a financial advisor for professional athletes. During COVID, he moved into real estate, specializing in finding homes for athletes instead.

It has been revealed that sangaré explains that the pros tend to make a lot of money for a short period of time, and for that reason they’re usually interested in buying investment properties (often right after they’ve found homes for themselves and their family members). A big part of their real estate agents’ job, then, is to keep their eyes on investment properties with the potential for strong returns.

Athletes have specific needs. “As a rookie, they’re just starting out, and they may not want to buy,” Sangaré told Taylor Anderson at eXpcon in Salt Lake City last month. Depending on the length of the contract, a rental might be a better idea. “There are times you tell people now’s not the right time to buy. If they feel you’re working in their best interests, they will trust you,” mentioned Sangaré, who is part of eXp’s relatively upcoming sports and entertainment division (which several brokerages offer).

You have to be patient when working with athletes, he stated, since their situations are tied to ever-changing contracts; of course, players can be traded, and have to move rapidly. You also have to be prepared to wait and work with them as they grow in their careers.

In a recent development, what you don’t have to be: A major follower of their particular sports. Sangaré admits that as a European, he doesn’t know much about football or baseball, but that doesn’t stop him from working with athletes in those sports. Sometimes not being starstruck helps him work with a more level head, he remarked.

But you do need to know the nuances of sports contracts. For example, some leagues, like the NBA, offer several-year guarantees, while others, like the NFL, don’t; housing options will vary based on those.

According to recent reports, often the connection to an athlete client comes through their financial advisor or sports agent, Sangaré said. “The sports agent is always talking to the player, and he’ll know to reach out to you when someone gets traded,” he said.

But that can be a long road. Sangaré said it can take anywhere from five months to two years from starting a relationship with a sports agent to seeing any traction with a player, but you want to start that relationship early since once their clients do start to get traded, they’ll undoubtedly be approached by many other real estate agents. One practical tip he gives is going to the NBA Summer League in Las Vegas and taking agents out for coffee or lunch. “You have to be present where they’re present,” he said.

According to recent reports, and when you do get connected to the client, make sure you don’t start with a sales pitch. “You can’t try to sell them something right away,” Sangaré mentioned; instead, you want to counsel them on how they can protect themselves and what they really need to know when buying a home — whether as an investment property or to live in.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Recognition honors Jacobsen's invention of reciprocal deposits and nearly 25 years of innovation, helping banks compete and serve their communities.

It has been revealed that ARLINGTON, Va., Nov. 24, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Mark P. Jacobsen, Cofounder and CEO of IntraFi, was named the EY Entrepreneur Of The YearÂ® 2026 National Award winner in the Financial Services category, recognizing his pioneering contributions to the banking industry and his leadership in building the nation's largest reciprocal deposit network.

The recognition celebrates Jacobsen's contributions to helping community and regional banks attract and retain deposits, allowing them to grant access for their customers to aggregate higher levels of FDIC insurance coverage and enabling them to better serve their communities.

Sources indicate that nearly 25 years ago, Jacobsen recognized a challenge facing community banks and their customers. Businesses and municipalities often needed to maintain deposits exceeding traditional FDIC insurance limits, while smaller banks struggled to compete with larger institutions for those relationships.

It has been revealed that jacobsen "conceived the idea of reciprocal deposits," wrote EY in its recognition. "IntraFi created an entirely fresh banking product.".

Sources indicate that reciprocal deposit services allow community banks to place uninsured deposits through a deposit placement network in increments below FDIC insurance limits and receive a matching amount of insured deposits in return. This allows small businesses, public funds and nonprofits to obtain higher levels of aggregate FDIC insurance. This benefits both the bank and its customers, allowing depositors to have a single relationship with their preferred institution while the bank can use the full amount of the deposit to fuel economic growth.

"Jacobsen brought the idea to life by combining a regulator's understanding of the financial system and an entrepreneur's instinct to challenge conventional thinking, plus the resolve to see the challenge through," mentioned EY, noting Jacobsen's former role as the chief of staff of two federal banking regulators. "He earned a dozen patents and worked with all the federal banking agencies as well as state and local governments, prompting more than 40 state laws to enable the use of reciprocal deposits.".

Today, IntraFi operates the nation's largest reciprocal deposit network, connecting more than 3,000 financial institutions, the vast majority of which are community banks. IntraFi's scale, sophisticated infrastructure, and proven reliability distinguish it from other providers, with established systems that have supported banks through multiple financial crises and periods of market stress.

Industry observers note that "Any recognition belongs solely to the employees of IntraFi and the thousands of banks that have put their faith in us," mentioned Jacobsen. Investment firm Roundhill has suddenly terminated intends to launch two latest XRP- and Solana (SOL)-based exchange-traded funds (ETFs).

This decision comes after over a year of regulatory filings and multiple delays.

Recent findings suggest that as per the U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC) filings on Nov. 18, Roundhill has officially withdrawn intends to launch the Roundhill XRP Covered Call Strategy ETF and Roundhill Solana Covered Call Strategy ETF.

According to recent reports, interestingly, it submitted the applications for these two funds on Oct. 17, 2025. Therefore, these two funds had been awaiting launch for over 13 months.

As per the latest regulatory filings, Roundhill has been consistently delaying the effective dates for these two funds.

However, instead of launching them, the investment firm has decided to drop both products.

In its requests to withdraw the filings for these funds, Roundhill revealed that it "has no further intention to pursue effectiveness of the Fund." The firm noted that it had not sold any shares under the registrations for these two funds.

Intriguingly, Roundhill failed to elaborate on the sudden decision to axe its aims to launch these two ETFs.

According to recent reports, roundhill was planning to launch income-generating XRP and Solana ETFs using a covered call strategy. In such a strategy, investors sell options to earn premiums while also maintaining exposure to the price movements of XRP and Solana.

Industry observers note that unlike spot-based ETFs, these funds would not have held the cryptocurrencies directly. Instead, they would have used options written against existing cryptocurrency ETFs.

A covered call strategy can be useful for generating regular income. However, it can also cap profits during strong market rallies.

Notably, there has been relatively low demand for income-generating cryptocurrency investment products. This raises concerns about investors' interest in these ETFs.

Surprisingly, this decision came amid substantial net inflows into spot-based XRP and Solana ETFs.

U.S. spot XRP and Solana ETFs recorded net inflows of roughly $969 million between May and October 2026, according to data from SoSoValue.

Overall, these spot ETFs held around $3.26 billion in assets under management as of the end of October.

Jeff Bezos has a space tech giant, a newspaper, an AI startup that’s raised $14.5 billion and, apparently, a seat in the room when Amazon decides who gets a license to kill.

Speaking Tuesday at Semafor’s Silicon Valley & The World event, the Amazon founder remarked he was “heavily involved” in the casting of Robert Pattinson as the next James Bond, a pick Amazon MGM Studios announced Monday.

In a recent development, amazon got a 50% stake in the Bond franchise when it acquired MGM for $8.5 billion in 2022, then took creative control last year in a joint venture with longtime producers Barbara Broccoli and Michael G. Wilson.

Bezos mentioned a large initial pool of would-be Bonds was narrowed to five finalists, who then did “real old-fashioned screen tests”: three scenes apiece, in full costume on real sets with other actors.

The other finalists were Nicholas Hoult, Jack Lowden, Josh O’Connor and Callum Turner, according to The New York Times, which reported that the tests took place in London in late October.

Bezos said the decision-makers got together Friday and spent a couple of hours reviewing the screen tests before settling on Pattinson.

In a recent development, “By the time we got to this list of five, they were all amazing,” Bezos noted. “But there was something special about Rob Pattinson and his performances.” He said the group, including director Denis Villeneuve, reached a quick consensus. It was “kind of immediately undebated.”.

Bezos admitted that the group was initially “slightly biased” against Pattinson because he’s already so famous.

According to recent reports, “We sort of thought, you know, maybe we should have somebody a little more unknown,” he mentioned. “But in the screen tests, it was so obvious he is James Bond.”.

#111307. Sometimes the most valuable data is the house nobody bought

📅 13 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 4m • 📚 Deep Dive (816 w)
📖 Baca
General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Inman ↗ Open Full Page

Sometimes the most valuable data is the house nobody bought

📅 13 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (816 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Inman

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Recent findings suggest that want to price more precisely?
  • It has been revealed that when agents sit down to price a listing, we know the drill: Pull the solds.
  • But there’s another category of data sitting right there in the MLS that we frequently overlook: the houses nobody bought.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Recent findings suggest that want to price more precisely? Canceled listing data in the MLS can reveal where buyers stated no. Learn three steps to add failed listings to your next CMA.

It has been revealed that when agents sit down to price a listing, we know the drill: Pull the solds. Look at what’s coming soon, active and pending. Adjust for condition, location, square footage and amenities. Figure out where our house fits.

But there’s another category of data sitting right there in the MLS that we frequently overlook: the houses nobody bought.

Expired. Canceled. Withdrawn. Earlier in my career, I looked at these failed listings all the time. Then the market changed. When inventory became tight, and buyers were competing for homes, digging through failed listings often wasn’t necessary to determine where a property would sell.

Now the market is shifting again; pricing must be more precise, and I’m sharpening my approach by bringing an old tool back into my pricing process.

A sold comp tells us where a buyer said yes, but a failed listing can help us figure out where buyers said no. And in a buyer-favored market, that’s valuable information.

According to recent reports, imagine you’re pricing a home, and the recent comparable sales range from $600,000 to $625,000. Then you expand your search.

Sources indicate that suddenly, you know considerably more than the sold comps alone told you. Other sellers have already tested the upper limits of pricing, and buyers responded. It’s essentially a series of pricing experiments someone else conducted for you — and they paid the carrying costs.

One of the most interesting things buried in MLS history is the pricing journey. A property might show a final list price of $649,000 and an eventual sale of $630,000. Dig deeper, and you may discover this:.

$725,000 → $699,000 → $675,000 → canceled → relisted at $649,000 → sold for $630,000.

That’s a different story. The sale tells us what one buyer eventually paid. The listing history tells us buyers had previously rejected that house at $725,000, $699,000 and $675,000.

Sources indicate that it also illustrates something sellers don’t always understand: Getting to the right price eventually isn’t necessarily the same as pricing correctly from the beginning. After months of market exposure and multiple reductions, buyers may stop asking, “Could this be the house?” They start asking, “What’s wrong with it?”.

In a recent development, when I find a comparable property that sat for 90 days without selling, I want to know what did sell during those same 90 days. Sometimes we blame the market when the market was functioning just fine. Buyers were buying houses. They simply weren’t buying that one.

Maybe they chose the renovated house at $640,000. Maybe they paid $650,000 for the better lot. They may have even paid more for another property because it offered something the failed listing didn’t. That’s useful information when you’re sitting across from a seller who believes buyers just need more time to appreciate their home.

If buyers repeatedly toured the property and purchased competing homes instead, the market may already have delivered its opinion.

This is where agents have to resist oversimplifying the data. An expired listing isn’t automatic proof that a house was overpriced, and a canceled listing certainly isn’t either.

Listings fail for all sorts of reasons. Sellers change their minds. Job transfers fall through. Repairs surface. Agents get fired. Sometimes a seller receives a perfectly acceptable offer and decides not to move.

Sources indicate that so, investigate. Call the previous agent. I might simply say:.

“I’m pricing a similar property and noticed yours was on the market last year. Is there anything you can tell me about the activity or why the seller decided not to continue?”.

Industry observers note that twenty-seven showings and no offers tell me something. Two showings in four months tells me something different.

There’s one more number worth considering: the cost of the pricing journey.

Find a house that started high, sat, reduced, expired, relisted and eventually sold. Then compare it with similar homes that entered the market closer to where buyers were actually buying.

According to recent reports, sellers often view aspirational pricing as a no-risk strategy: “We can always come down.” Technically, that’s true. But time isn’t free, and neither is market perception.

The next time you’re preparing a CMA in a shifting or buyer-favored market:.

We’re very good at studying success in real estate. But as pricing gets harder, I’ve found myself returning to an old habit: studying the failures, too. Sold listings tell us where buyers have been willing to say yes. Sometimes the house nobody bought is the one that tells us exactly where they started saying no.

Roxanne Hale is the associate broker of the Art House Team, brokered by RealtySouth in Birmingham, Alabama. Get connected on Facebook or YouTube.

While the total amount of SOL unstaked was worth about $169.4 million, further data demonstrated that the whales proceeded to transfer the tokens to Coinbase, a leading cryptocurrency exchange in the U.S.

It is notable to note that the act of withdrawing SOL previously committed to the network's staking mechanism is regarded as unstaking.

While this move automatically gives holders the ability to transfer, sell, or use the unstaked tokens, the massive unstaking of 2.31 million SOL from large holders has drawn attention within the crypto community regarding the intention behind the move.

With curiosity on the rise about the whales' decision to move such a large amount of SOL to Coinbase Prime, the timing of the move has triggered speculation that the whales may be intending to sell the tokens.

Notably, the move arrived when Solana was trading around $74, briefly shifting into green territory just a few days after it retested $67, the lowest level seen since June 2026.

Since the prolonged price correction has continued to weaken investor confidence, it appears that the whales have acted upon the growing fear and withdrawn the assets they had initially committed to the Solana network to hedge against further losses.

Breaking: Mortgage application payments reveal slight homebuyer affordability gain in October

📅 24 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 2 min read (493 words, 📖 Standard) | Source: Housingwire

⏱️ ~2 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Homebuyer affordability improved slightly in October as lower purchase loan amounts offset higher mortgage rates, according to the Mortgage Bankers Association (MBA)’s Purchase Applications Payment Index (PAPI), released Tuesday.
  • The index, which measures mortgage payments relative to borrower income, decreased 0.3% to a reading of 161.6 in October, down from 162.1 in September.
  • The improvement came despite the national median mortgage payment for purchase applicants rising to $2,236 in October, up $21 (or 0.9%) from $2,215 in September.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Homebuyer affordability improved slightly in October as lower purchase loan amounts offset higher mortgage rates, according to the Mortgage Bankers Association (MBA)’s Purchase Applications Payment Index (PAPI), released Tuesday.

The index, which measures mortgage payments relative to borrower income, decreased 0.3% to a reading of 161.6 in October, down from 162.1 in September. A lower index reading indicates improving affordability.

The improvement came despite the national median mortgage payment for purchase applicants rising to $2,236 in October, up $21 (or 0.9%) from $2,215 in September. The median purchase loan application amount fell to $315,424 from $324,022, helping offset a 37-basis-point increase in mortgage rates.

“While the median mortgage payment rose $21 in October, payments as a share of earnings edged lower — slightly improving affordability,” Edward Seiler, MBA’s associate vice president of housing economics and executive director of the Research Institute for Housing America, mentioned in a statement.

Affordability remains weaker than a year ago. The median mortgage payment increased 9.7% from $2,039 in October 2025, while earnings grew 1.6%. As a result, the PAPI was up 8% year over year.

“Looking ahead, lower mortgage rates and stronger earnings growth would give prospective buyers more room in their budgets,” Seiler said.

In a recent development, the median mortgage payment for Federal Housing Administration (FHA) borrowers increased to $1,944 in October, up from $1,906 in September and $1,789 a year earlier. For conventional loan borrowers, the median payment rose to $2,258, up from $2,244 in September and $2,063 in October 2025.

Among borrowers applying for lower-payment mortgages, those in the 25th percentile, the median monthly payment increased to $1,536 in October from $1,525 in September.

The PAPI for Black households decreased to 162.4 in October from 162.9 in September. For Hispanic households, it fell to 149.6 from 150.1, while the index for white households declined to 162.8 from 163.3.

Idaho had the highest PAPI reading in October at 269.8, followed by Nevada at 243.0, Rhode Island at 233.1, Arizona at 215.2 and Utah at 202.7. At the opposite end of the spectrum, Louisiana had the lowest reading at 119.8, followed by Washington, D.C., at 121.5, Alaska at 126.2, Iowa at 127.6 and Connecticut at 131.6.

Sources indicate that the MBA’s mortgage payment-to-rent ratio also edged higher, increasing to 1.44 at the end of the third quarter from 1.43 at the end of the second quarter. The increase indicates that mortgage payments for home purchases rose slightly relative to rents.

The U.S. Census Bureau reported that the national median asking rent increased to $1,541 in the third quarter from $1,531 in the second quarter. The ratio of mortgage payments for lower-payment applicants to median asking rents remained at 0.99 in September.

Separately, the MBA’s Builders’ PAPI showed that the median mortgage payment for fresh-home purchase applicants increased to $2,375 in October, up from $2,307 in September.

This article was generated using HousingWire Automation and reviewed by a HousingWire editor before publication.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • by Lisa Stiffler on Nov 17, 2026 at 11:00 pmNovember 18, 2026 at 7:47 am.
  • Sila, a startup producing next-generation battery materials, announced a long-term customer agreement with Panasonic Energy Corporation of North America potentially worth more than $1 billion.
  • It has been revealed that panasonic, a battery supplier to Tesla, will buy Sila’s Titan Silicon anode material for its U.S.-made battery cells.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

by Lisa Stiffler on Nov 17, 2026 at 11:00 pmNovember 18, 2026 at 7:47 am.

Sila, a startup producing next-generation battery materials, announced a long-term customer agreement with Panasonic Energy Corporation of North America potentially worth more than $1 billion. To meet demand from Panasonic and other buyers, the organization prepares to expand its plant in Moses Lake, Wash., supporting roughly 500 additional manufacturing and construction jobs over the coming years.

It has been revealed that panasonic, a battery supplier to Tesla, will buy Sila’s Titan Silicon anode material for its U.S.-made battery cells. The silicon-carbon composite can replace some or all of the graphite in lithium-ion battery anodes to improve performance.

Sila began operations at its Moses Lake plant last year and has about 100 full-time employees at the site. The facility is still scaling up production, with initial capacity designed to supply batteries totaling about 2 gigawatt-hours — enough for roughly 20,000 to 50,000 EVs, depending on how the material is used.

The expansion will increase that capacity to tens of gigawatt-hours, said Gene Berdichevsky, Sila’s co-founder and CEO.

“This is a really important blueprint for reindustrializing the U.S.,” he noted. “We have to take latest technology and leapfrog China, not just copy what they’ve done over the last 20 years.”.

While the U.S. has expanded battery manufacturing, it still depends heavily on overseas suppliers for core materials and technologies, Berdichevsky said. Sila aims to strengthen that domestic supply chain with higher-performing components.

Batteries support industries central to energy independence and national security. They power EVs, consumer devices, drones, robotics and hardware deployed in space, and provide backup electricity for data centers.

Berdichevsky said Titan Silicon can help a battery store 20%–40% more energy in the same space, cut recharging time roughly in half and deliver more power than a battery using a conventional graphite anode. The anode itself is also much lighter and smaller.

In August, Sila received a conditional federal loan commitment of up to $1.4 billion through the Pentagon’s Office of Strategic Capital to expand domestic battery technology manufacturing. The company must meet financial, legal, technical and other requirements before the loan can be finalized.

The startup previously received a $100 million grant during the Biden administration under a similar initiative to increase U.S. energy independence. Those funds helped build its plant in Washington.

The organization has also raised $1.6 billion from private investors, including a $300 million round announced in July. The 15-year-old company is valued at $2.27 billion, according to PitchBook.

Seattle-area startup Group14 also makes a silicon-carbon anode material. It operates a smaller-scale manufacturing facility at its Woodinville, Wash., headquarters and produces commercial-scale volumes at a plant in South Korea.

According to recent reports, group14 has partially completed its Moses Lake manufacturing site but repeatedly delayed the start of production. It now targets mid-2027 to bring the first of two production units online, with no firm completion date for the second. It recently announced plans for a factory in Spain.

Growth is key to bringing down costs and making Sila’s technology competitive in mass-market batteries, Berdichevsky stated.

“This is really the beginning of chapter three for our company’s history,” he said.

It has been revealed that the first two chapters were inventing the technology and moving from grams to tons of production, he added. This phase is about reaching the mass market. Sila aims to begin manufacturing at the expanded facility in 2028, with output increasing over time.

Sources indicate that “None of this is easy,” Berdichevsky mentioned. “It’s not the inventing technology; it’s the manufacturing of it that’s really really hard, and we’re going to try to more than 10x the scale from what we’ve already done.”.

Make it 8: Connecticut joins first responder homebuying push

📅 13 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (826 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Inman

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Connecticut is the latest state to help first responders reach their homeownership goals with assistance for down payments and closing costs.
  • The “First Responders’ Time to Own” program gives state and local police officers, full-time and volunteer firefighters and emergency medical service personnel $25,000 in forgivable assistance through the Connecticut Housing Finance Authority (CHFA) and the Connecticut Department of Housing.
  • In addition to down payment and closing cost help, the program gives applicants a 0.125 percentage point interest rate reduction on their CHFA first mortgage.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Connecticut is the latest state to help first responders reach their homeownership goals with assistance for down payments and closing costs.

The “First Responders’ Time to Own” program gives state and local police officers, full-time and volunteer firefighters and emergency medical service personnel $25,000 in forgivable assistance through the Connecticut Housing Finance Authority (CHFA) and the Connecticut Department of Housing. To qualify, first responders must have completed two years of service and purchase a primary residence within the community they serve.

In addition to down payment and closing cost help, the program gives applicants a 0.125 percentage point interest rate reduction on their CHFA first mortgage.

“Connecticut’s police officers, firefighters and EMS personnel dedicate themselves to protecting our families and communities, and we want to make sure they have the opportunity to build their own futures here,” Governor Ned Lamont said in a prepared statement on Tuesday. “By helping reduce one of the biggest barriers to buying a home, we’re investing in the people who serve our state and the communities that depend on them.”.

The program is part of Public Act 26-12, a state bill that aims to increase the number of first responders with a number of incentives, including college tuition reimbursement and improved labor protections.

According to recent reports, “The people who protect and serve our communities should be able to afford to live in those communities, and this program with help them do it,” Comptroller Sean Scanlon remarked in a written statement. “Helping the people who put their lives on the line for us every day buy their first home is literally the least we can do, and I’m proud to have worked with Governor Lamont and legislature to make this a reality.”.

Recent findings suggest that seven other states also have down payment assistance programs for first responders. Florida, Nevada, Georgia and South Carolina provide flat amounts, ranging from $10,000 to $35,000. Texas, Maryland and Ohio’s programs are percentage-based and offer assistance ranging from 2.5 percent to 5 percent of the purchase price.

The terms of each program vary. Most states forgive the assistance after five to seven years, but Nevada requires homebuyers to repay the funds within 30 years. And like Connecticut, Ohio also offers a 0.25 percent mortgage rate discount.

According to recent reports, “Homeownership offers more than a place to live. It creates stability, strengthens connections to community and provides an opportunity to build wealth over time,” CHFA CEO and Executive Director Nandini Natarajan said in an announcement. “Through First Responders’ Time to Own, we’re helping the people who answer the call for our communities take an crucial step toward achieving their own homeownership goals.”.

First responders often fall through the cracks of housing assistance programs because they don’t earn enough to afford market-rate housing but earn too much to qualify for federal housing vouchers.

Industry observers note that inman explored this dilemma last September in a feature on workforce housing in resort towns like Jackson Hole, Vail and Tahoe. These towns can’t operate without first responders and other essential workers in the hospitality and retail sectors. However, rental and for-sale home prices have far outpaced what these workers earn, forcing them to commute long distances from more affordable towns or take on second and third jobs to survive.

Sources indicate that the solution for some of these towns has been investing in workforce housing, which caps prices for households that earn between 60 percent and 120 percent of their area’s AMI. Most workforce housing is rent-only, but some states are extending the programs to include for-sale properties.

“I think the fact that workforce housing can be necessary or is a thing in the first place is really an indictment of the state of housing affordability in the country today,” Realtor.com Senior Economist Jake Krimmel said. “I think it’s notable to ground any conversation about workforce and affordable housing in that reality. It’s a market failure and a policy failure that someone could be a doctor, a teacher or another kind of professional and cannot afford to pay the market rent or own a home outright.”.

Windermere Principal Economist Jeff Tucker noted workforce housing isn’t a panacea for affordability and works within an ecosystem of other housing and economic policies, such as upzoning, to create a more equitable market.

According to recent reports, tucker’s comments came a month after the Senate introduced the ROAD to Housing Act of 2025, and three months before the House introduced the Housing for the 21st Century Act. The bills were eventually combined into the 21st Century ROAD to Housing Act, which passed in June.

“A broad package of necessary reforms to make more housing construction possible in much of the country is a really important component of a long-term solution to the housing affordability challenges we face,” Tucker stated. “Our current housing shortage took years to develop. So it’ll take years to build our way out of it.”.

#111299. Lower mortgage rates could bring buyers back. What market will they return to?

📅 24 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 6m • 📚 Deep Dive (1125 w)
📖 Baca
Business & Policy ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Housingwire ↗ Open Full Page

Lower mortgage rates could bring buyers back. What market will they return to?

📅 24 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 6 min read (1125 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Housingwire

⏱️ ~6 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • The possibility of mortgage rates falling below 7% before the holidays is back on the table.
  • But for housing professionals hoping to reengage buyers who stepped away from the market, mortgage rates are only part of the equation.
  • The homes available, the prices sellers are asking and the competition buyers face may look considerably different from when those buyers last searched.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

The possibility of mortgage rates falling below 7% before the holidays is back on the table. In Tuesday morning’s Analyst Insights revision in HousingWire Intelligence, HousingWire Lead Analyst Logan Mohtashami noted that the 10-year Treasury yield had reached 4.89%, approaching the 4.85% threshold he is watching, though mortgage spreads still need to improve.

But for housing professionals hoping to reengage buyers who stepped away from the market, mortgage rates are only part of the equation.

The homes available, the prices sellers are asking and the competition buyers face may look considerably different from when those buyers last searched.

Nationally, active single-family inventory stands at 894,692 homes, approximately 8% higher than a year ago. Fresh pending listings increased 5.7% in the week ending Nov. 20, while new listings increased 1.2%.

That increase in contract activity is encouraging, but the broader picture remains more complicated.

HousingWire Data highlights that 44 of 57 large metro areas (77.2%) recorded an improving ratio of new pending listings to new listings over consecutive four-week periods, even as pending activity remained below year-ago levels.

During the comparable period in 2025, just three of 54 qualifying metros (5.6%) revealed that same combination.

Sources indicate that an improving relationship between incoming listings and fresh contracts does not necessarily indicate strengthening buyer demand. And if lower mortgage rates do bring buyers back, the opportunities they encounter will vary considerably by market.

Consider Denver and Kansas City, two metro areas averaging nearly identical numbers of new pending listings per week but offering buyers different inventory and pricing environments.

Over the four weeks ending Nov. 20, Denver averaged 497 upcoming pending listings per week, while Kansas City averaged 491. Both markets are experiencing substantially weaker contract activity than a year ago.

That’s where the similarities begin to fade.

Denver’s housing market offers buyers a different landscape heading into the holidays, with more available inventory, lower asking prices than during the spring and widespread price reductions.

For buyers who paused their home searches earlier this year because of affordability, Denver’s changing inventory and pricing conditions provide a reason to revisit their options, even before mortgage rates move meaningfully lower.

Kansas City’s median asking price has declined from its summer peak as price reductions have become more prevalent, although median asking prices remain above year-ago levels.

Kansas City offers buyers considerably more selection than a year ago. And while asking prices have moderated since the summer, higher median asking prices compared with last year could offset some of the affordability gains from lower borrowing costs.

Both markets offer more available homes than a year ago, but the pricing environments are different.

In a recent development, in Denver, a decline in mortgage rates could coincide with lower asking prices and more available homes. In Kansas City, greater selection and recent pricing adjustments may create opportunities, even though the median asking price remains higher than it was a year ago.

According to recent reports, changes in median asking prices can reflect shifts in the composition of available inventory, not just changes in individual home prices. That’s why examining inventory, asking prices and price reductions together provides a more useful assessment of local buying conditions than any one metric alone.

Another consideration is whether contract activity is already beginning to strengthen, even with mortgage rates above 7%.

In Denver, weekly new pending listings increased across the four most recent reporting weeks:.

Cincinnati, Ohio, recorded a similar pattern, with weekly new pending listings increasing from 397 to 459 over the same period.

In a recent development, but Cincinnati presents a different inventory and pricing environment. Its median active list price is up 1.9% year over year, and the market has 2.44 months of inventory, compared with 3.01 in Denver.

While both markets have recorded three consecutive weekly increases in contract activity, buyers returning to Cincinnati could encounter a tighter inventory environment than those returning to Denver.

Neither market has recovered to last year’s level of contract activity, and several weeks of increases are not enough to establish a sustained recovery, particularly heading into the holidays.

Still, these are developments worth monitoring. If contract activity continues to strengthen while new listings decline seasonally, competition for available homes could increase.

Housing professionals don’t need to wait for mortgage rates to fall below 7% to start preparing for that possibility.

The more immediate opportunity is to understand how local market conditions have changed since buyers last evaluated their options.

For buyer’s agents: Revisit the searches of clients who paused their homebuying intends earlier this year. Has available inventory expanded in their price range? Are more homes experiencing price reductions? Changing market conditions may create opportunities worth exploring before rates move lower.

For listing agents: More available inventory means more competition for sellers. Monitor new pending listings alongside active inventory and price reductions to help sellers evaluate whether their pricing strategy remains competitive as buyer activity changes.

Industry observers note that for mortgage lenders: Reengaging prospective purchase borrowers doesn’t have to begin with a conversation about mortgage rates. Understanding how available homes and asking prices have changed in a borrower’s target market can help make that conversation more relevant. Revisit purchasing power using current local asking prices and different mortgage rate scenarios.

For brokerage leaders: National mortgage rate movements can provide a reason to launch buyer reengagement campaigns, but local housing conditions should inform the messaging. A market with expanding inventory and declining asking prices presents a different opportunity than one with tighter inventory and strengthening contract activity.

Using HousingWire Intelligence, you can recreate the charts above for your own metro area, city or ZIP code.

Select single-family homes, choose the one-year view and examine four metrics together:.

Use the one-year view to understand seasonal patterns, then narrow your analysis to the most recent three or six months to identify changes in market conditions.

Looking at these metrics together can help you distinguish between a market offering greater selection and potential affordability opportunities and one where renewed buyer activity could increase competition for available homes.

Mortgage rates may give buyers a reason to reconsider their plans. Understanding how local market conditions have changed gives housing professionals a reason to reach out before they do.

Source: HousingWire Data. Metro-level analysis reflects single-family housing data using four-week averages through Nov. 20, 2026, and comparable periods in 2025. The national weekly figures reflect the week ending Nov. 20. Large metro areas were defined as those with at least 3,000 average active listings and 100 average weekly upcoming pending listings. Qualifying metro areas may differ between comparison periods. New pending listings represent homes entering contract, not closed transactions. Median active list prices reflect asking prices and may be influenced by changes in the composition of available inventory.

Tech Report: ‘Absurd ambition’: Pulumi expands into software delivery with AI agents that ship and fix code

📅 18 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 6 min read (1121 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Geekwire

⏱️ ~6 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • by Todd Bishop on Nov 18, 2026 at 8:57 amNovember 18, 2026 at 9:01 am.
  • Cloud-infrastructure startup Pulumi has a name for its current fiscal year, which started in July: “the year of absurd ambition.” The first results arrived Wednesday: two products the Seattle company talked about building for years but always found too substantial to take on.
  • The products, Pulumi Delivery and Pulumi Agents, let AI agents take over more of the work of getting new software up and running, and fixing it when something breaks.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

by Todd Bishop on Nov 18, 2026 at 8:57 amNovember 18, 2026 at 9:01 am.

Cloud-infrastructure startup Pulumi has a name for its current fiscal year, which started in July: “the year of absurd ambition.” The first results arrived Wednesday: two products the Seattle company talked about building for years but always found too substantial to take on.

The products, Pulumi Delivery and Pulumi Agents, let AI agents take over more of the work of getting new software up and running, and fixing it when something breaks.

It has been revealed that “The ceiling on what we can accomplish is no longer limited by the speed at which we can build software,” remarked Joe Duffy, the tech giant’s co-founder and CEO, recounting the message he delivered to the Pulumi team. “It’s limited by how ambitious we’re willing to be and how major we’re willing to dream.”.

In a recent development, the ambition is all the more notable because Pulumi is getting smaller. The company has about 100 employees, down from about 130 last year. Duffy said there were no layoffs, and that AI has changed people’s roles and made the company more efficient.

In a recent development, annual recurring revenue per employee more than doubled over the past year, he said. The organization isn’t profitable yet, but it has had a few months of positive cash flow this year. Pulumi hasn’t raised money since 2023, when it landed a $41 million round led by Madrona, bringing its total to about $99 million over the company’s lifetime.

Industry observers note that pulumi’s co-founders include Duffy and Eric Rudder, both Microsoft veterans. They started the manufacturer in 2017 to let engineers manage cloud infrastructure such as servers, networks and permissions by writing code in everyday languages like Python and TypeScript.

The latest products take that approach further:.

To decide whether a change is safe to ship, Pulumi Delivery can use Jev, an AI model from TypeSafe AI that estimates the odds of specific risks the team asks about in a planned change. If a risk is higher than the threshold the team sets, the release stops.

In a recent development, duffy noted he first noticed TypeSafe in May when it signed up as a Pulumi customer, because he liked the name. A few months later, Jev took off and TypeSafe used Pulumi to expand worldwide.

“Now even the call on whether a change ships can be made by a model,” said Daniel Gafni, a member of the technical staff at TypeSafe AI, in the Pulumi announcement. “That’s exactly the kind of decision we built Jev to make.”.

According to recent reports, both products are available now in public preview. Some features, including Jev decision gates and setting up agents, require Pulumi’s paid Pro or Enterprise plans.

Lucky timing: Pulumi’s founding bet on everyday programming languages turned out to suit AI agents, which are trained to be very good at writing exactly that kind of code.

“I wish I could say I predicted that 10 years ago, but it turns out in this case, what’s good for humans is also good for agents,” Duffy mentioned.

AI agents now handle 40% of the operations on the Pulumi platform that people used to do, up from 15% in April and none in January, Duffy stated. Agents such as Claude Code, Codex and Pulumi’s own Neo are making infrastructure changes on their own.

Industry observers note that duffy noted many companies building AI coding tools stop once the code is written and reviewed. “For them, life stops at the merge,” he said. The fresh products cover the steps after that, from testing through release.

Plenty of company: Pulumi won’t have this market to itself. Duffy pointed to Harness, which calls it the “agentic SDLC” (short for software development lifecycle), and GitHub, which pitched “agentic software delivery” at its Universe conference last month. He said Cursor aspires to solve the problem and Anthropic built its own internal system.

The new products could replace some of the work now done by tools such as Argo CD and GitHub Actions, along with lots of homegrown scripts, he said.

Sources indicate that “This is an industry-changing moment, and somebody has to solve this problem,” Duffy noted. “And I think we are exceptionally well poised to do so.”.

Recent findings suggest that bring your own bot: Neo, the infrastructure agent Pulumi introduced last year, is now just one example of a Pulumi agent. Customers can set up as many as they want, each with its own job, instructions and tools. They can also bring their own agent, such as Claude Code or Codex, and run it in Pulumi’s cloud.

Neo itself, which ran mainly on Anthropic’s Claude, can now use models from OpenAI or Google, too. “It’s not just Anthropic anymore,” Duffy mentioned.

Agents can start work from an alert in PagerDuty, Datadog or Honeycomb, on a schedule or on request, and they report back to teams in Slack.

It has been revealed that pulumi has briefed about 50 customers, and about a dozen are in a private beta. Duffy stated no launch in the company’s history has gotten a warmer reception, and he named Moderna among the customers eager to get it.

Pulumi has thousands of customers overall, including major companies such as BMW, Snowflake and Wiz.

Sources indicate that the business: Pulumi’s gross margins have stayed in the high 80s to low 90s even as agents drive up usage, Duffy said. Many customers run Pulumi from inside their own Claude Code sessions, which means they’re paying both Anthropic and Pulumi.

Duffy said Pulumi wasn’t out looking for money when it raised its last two rounds. Investors came to the company, and each deal came together in about 48 hours.

Madrona’s Tim Porter has joined the board, Duffy stated, taking the seat previously held by the late Soma Somasegar, who led Pulumi’s first investment.

About 40 of the firm’s 100 employees are in the Seattle area, working out of an office at Two Union Square. Duffy said Pulumi is hiring more people locally because in-person work still matters when building fresh products.

Despite the smaller headcount, Pulumi is still hiring, including sales reps in nearly every region of the world. Inside the firm, Duffy said Pulumi is having a lot of success with “product-minded engineers who can think from our customers’ point of view, who can think like engineering managers, commanding a team of agents.”.

Asked whether a sale or more funding was in the cards, Duffy mentioned Pulumi aspires to be a long-term successful business. “There are a variety of ways to get there,” he said. “But we want to get there on our own terms.”.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It has been revealed that leading cryptocurrency exchange Coinbase has announced the official listing of artificial intelligence (AI) giant Anthropic (ANT) shares on its trading platform in the U.S. and U.K.

According to recent reports, the listing comes as Anthropic, the manufacturer behind the popular AI chatbot Claude, officially made its much-anticipated stock market debut on Thursday, Nov. 19, with its shares seeing massive volatility.

According to recent reports, as per the latest X post from Coinbase, the exchange revealed the availability of Anthropic (ANT) shares for eligible people in the U.S. and U.K.

It has been revealed that it's important to mention that ANT isn't a cryptocurrency but a traditional stock. Coinbase's support for ANT shares demonstrates the tech giant's efforts to expand its offerings beyond crypto into traditional financial markets.

Anthropic has set a latest historic precedent, having successfully raised about $81 billion in its initial public offering (IPO). This is the biggest IPO ever.

The artificial intelligence company sold 980 million shares at $83 per share, significantly higher than its previously confirmed price range of $70 to $78.

This brought Anthropic's initial valuation to about $1.5 trillion, making the firm one of the most valuable publicly listed firms in the world right from the get-go.

But as Anthropic shares started trading on the Nasdaq exchange, the ANT ticker saw massive volatility.

As per Reuters, Anthropic shares began trading at $111.50. This represented an enormous 34% premium over the IPO price.

At the initial peak, Anthropic's market cap exceeded $2 trillion, surpassing SpaceX's valuation when it debuted on the market in June.

Sources indicate that anthropic shares slipped to around $95 as the stock gave back a significant chunk of its gains. This was partly due to investors looking to book their profits.

Nonetheless, Anthropic shares were still trading comfortably above their $83 IPO price.

The volatility surrounding Anthropic's stock market debut signals increasing doubts about the AI investment craze.

The listing of Anthropic shares is just one of Coinbase's moves to enter traditional financial markets.

Instead of just providing cryptocurrency trading, the exchange is looking to become a platform for multiple asset classes.

Recent findings suggest that interestingly, Coinbase had already listed Anthropic pre-IPO perpetual futures for eligible non-U.S. users on Nov. 18.

The perpetual futures were derivative contracts that allowed traders to speculate on Anthropic's valuation before its shares officially started trading on Nasdaq.

It has been revealed that with the latest listing, eligible Coinbase users in the U.S. and U.K. can now trade the publicly listed Anthropic shares.

Anthropic's blockbuster debut comes as financial markets have been rocked by recent volatility, with tech stocks and crypto facing selling pressure.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Shares of human resources and finance software tech giant Workday Inc.
  • 31, Workday reported adjusted earnings per share of $2.82, up 22% from $2.32 in the same quarter of the previous year, on revenue of $2.705 billion, up 11.2% year-over-year.
  • Recent findings suggest that subscription revenue rose 12.8% from a year earlier, to $2.532 billion.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

UPDATED 17:27 EST / NOVEMBER 24 2026.

Shares of human resources and finance software tech giant Workday Inc. fell more than 7% in late trading today after a softer-than-expected subscription revenue forecast for the current quarter overshadowed fiscal third-quarter earnings and revenue that came in ahead of Wall Street’s targets.

For the quarter that ended on Oct. 31, Workday reported adjusted earnings per share of $2.82, up 22% from $2.32 in the same quarter of the previous year, on revenue of $2.705 billion, up 11.2% year-over-year. Analysts were expecting earnings of $2.75 per share on revenue of $2.69 billion.

Recent findings suggest that subscription revenue rose 12.8% from a year earlier, to $2.532 billion. Net income on an unadjusted basis came to $237 million, down from $252 million in the same quarter a year ago. Included in the quarter were $51 million in restructuring expenses, which followed the company’s disclosure in late September that it would cut about 2.5% of its workforce, mostly in its product and technology team.

Recent findings suggest that total subscription revenue backlog grew 6.1%, to $27.548 billion, with the 12-month figure up 12.3%, to $9.216 billion. Free cash flow came to $691 million, up from $550 million. During the quarter, Workday spent $750 million buying back about 3.8 million shares.

The quarter also saw Workday hold its annual Rising customer conference in Las Vegas in October, when the manufacturer made Sana the upcoming home experience for its platform. Built on technology from Sana Labs AB, which Workday acquired for about $1.1 billion last year, Sana is an AI interface that brings tasks, decisions, meetings and agent activity together in one place. Autopilot Agents, also launched at the event, are designed to handle routine HR, finance and IT processes in the background.

In a recent development, on the opening day of Rising, Workday revealed that it had agreed to acquire agentic identity platform ConductorOne Inc., better known as C1.ai. That deal closed on Monday. A partnership with Anthropic PBC, also unveiled at Rising, is set to bring Claude together with Sana AI agents and Workday’s HR and finance data.

“The past few quarters have been our strongest on the innovation and invention front, and in Q3, our AI products drove nearly $150 million in new ACV, more than three times what we delivered a year ago,” said co-founder and Chief Executive Aneel Bhusri, who returned to the top job in February after Carl Eschenbach stepped down. The priority now, Bhusri added, is to get more customers running agents in production.

According to Workday, the number of core customers that have bought at least one of its AI products rose nearly 25% from the previous quarter, to more than 2,200.

Pointing to what he called “ongoing adoption across our AI portfolio,” Chief Financial Officer Zane Rowe noted the company is raising its full-year targets.

In a recent development, for its fiscal fourth quarter, Workday expects subscription revenue of $2.6 billion, up 10%, and an adjusted operating margin of 31.7%. Full-year subscription revenue is now forecast at $9.958 billion, up 13%, compared with the $9.94 billion to $9.95 billion guided in August. The full-year adjusted operating margin forecast was also raised, to 31.5%, ahead of the 31.1% expected by analysts.

Though the full-year numbers moved higher, the fourth-quarter subscription forecast came in narrowly below the $2.61 billion analysts had been expecting. Growth of 10% in the period would also be a step down from the 12.8% Workday posted in the third quarter.

#111293. Your real estate listing is stuck and a price drop will not fix it

📅 24 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 5m • 📚 Deep Dive (999 w)
📖 Baca
General ⚠️ Warning 🌐 Housingwire ↗ Open Full Page

Your real estate listing is stuck and a price drop will not fix it

📅 24 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (999 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Housingwire

⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • There is a category of stuck listing that is going to become more common over the next few years, and most agents have not been trained for it.
  • This came up on one of our Power Agent coaching calls.
  • The building had a balcony and structural-compliance issue, the kind of inspection-and-repair requirement that has spread across the country since Surfside and that states like California have written into law for decks and balconies.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

There is a category of stuck listing that is going to become more common over the next few years, and most agents have not been trained for it. It is the listing that cannot sell for a reason that has nothing to do with price, photography or effort. It is the listing blocked at the building level, and if we keep coaching agents to treat every slow listing with a price reduction, we are going to watch good professionals burn good listings for no reason.

This came up on one of our Power Agent coaching calls. An agent brought me a four-unit situation. The condo had been on the market for 86 days. She had lost two solid buyers. One was all cash, and the all-cash buyer still walked. Any time an all-cash buyer walks, leaders should pay attention, because the one thing you cannot blame is financing.

The building had a balcony and structural-compliance issue, the kind of inspection-and-repair requirement that has spread across the country since Surfside and that states like California have written into law for decks and balconies. The repairs had not been started. A new management tech giant had taken over months earlier and was still, in their words, figuring things out.

Because the work was un-started, the building landed on the list that does not qualify for conventional Fannie Mae and Freddie Mac financing. The financed buyers were gone instantly. The all-cash buyer pulled the association financials, saw thin reserves and un-started repairs, read it correctly as a poorly run building, and decided the headache was not worth it.

Recent findings suggest that powerfact: Structural-compliance problems do not lower a home’s price. They remove a home’s buyers.

That distinction matters for anyone leading a team, because it changes the coaching. When a building cannot get conventional financing, the buyer pool does not shrink, it collapses to cash buyers willing to tolerate a troubled association. We just watched one of those rare buyers say no. Telling that agent to drop the price would have been coaching malpractice. The price was never the lever.

Here is the plan I gave her, and it is the plan I would want every leader teaching.

Take it off the market, temporarily. Days on market is a public number, and a climbing one negotiates against your seller before an offer is ever written. Pull the listing before the clock becomes the story.

Sources indicate that then, stay hired. This is the step that separates an advisor from an order-taker. Taking a listing off the market should not end the relationship, it should restructure it. The agent and I built a upcoming listing agreement long enough to cover the repair timeline plus fresh marketing afterward at a likely new price.

If repairs take a couple of months and the sale takes several more, that is an eight or nine month agreement, not a renewal of the old 90 days. The property comes off the MLS and is not shown, but the agreement stays active. The agent keeps her position. The seller keeps a professional who is still working.

It has been revealed that then, advocate for the whole building. I told her to get in front of the management tech giant and the association board, the president and the vice president, and push to expedite repairs that are hurting all 54 owners. This is where a top producer builds a reputation that compounds. When you are the agent pushing a stalled building back into compliance, every owner in that building knows your name, and so does every agent who tried and gave up. In a 54-unit building, that is 54 future listing conversations you just earned by being the one who showed up and did the work nobody else would touch.

Industry observers note that we also talked through the rent-instead question, because these sellers had already relocated and were carrying the unit. Renting for a year while the building gets sorted is a legitimate option, but it has to be coached with the worst case on the table. In a tenant-friendly jurisdiction an eviction can run six to nine months. Florida’s landlord rules are workable. Other markets are not.

This property sits in California, and I told her plainly that I do not know California’s specifics well enough to promise a timeline, so she needs to find out. Because if the tenant will not leave and removal takes six months, the one-year rental really delivered about six months of clean cash flow. Leaders, this is the kind of worst-case math we owe our sellers, and it is exactly the math an anxious agent skips to avoid an awkward conversation.

The larger point for the industry is this. Compliance-driven financing blocks are a growing reality, and they reward the agent who can diagnose, not just discount. The old reflex of lowering price until something moves does not clear a building-level obstacle, and agents who only know that one move will lose listings they could have saved. The professionals who win in this environment are the ones who can look a seller in the eye and say, the problem is not your price, the problem is your building, and here is the plan to fix it.

Industry observers note that that is the advisor our clients actually need. Serve, don’t sell. In a market with this much noise, the agent who clings to a dying listing looks desperate, and the one who calmly takes the sign out of the yard, extends the agreement, and goes to fix the real problem looks like exactly what they are. The one in control.

Industry observers note that darryl Davis, CSP, is a national speaker, real estate coach, and the bestselling author of How to Become a Power Agent® in Real Estate. Learn more at darrylspeaks.com.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Valuable Records are Available for Free Online.

SILVER SPRING, Md. , Nov. 24, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- The National Genealogical Society (NGS) is excited to share that the Preserve the Pensions project to digitize War of 1812 pension files is finished, and the files are now available to the public for free permanently with full-text search via Fold3.

Recent findings suggest that the culmination of sixteen years of fundraising and careful work to save deteriorating files and make them accessible online, this project provides genealogists and family historians with nearly three million pages of records from approximately 90,000 individual files. A partnership between NGS, Fold3, Ancestry, FamilySearch, and the National Archives and Records Administration (NARA), and contributions from people and organizations across the genealogy community, made this incredible endeavor possible and illustrate the power of collaboration.

Industry observers note that "After successfully raising the $2.7 million needed to conserve and digitize the War of 1812 pensions deposited with NARA in Washington, DC, we are thrilled that our digitization partner, Fold3, has completed digitizing the last box of pensions. This effort, originally initiated as a request from the National Archives, concludes the largest private/public partnership the genealogical community has had where donations led directly to making these invaluable records freely available," stated NGS President David E. Rencher, AG, CG, FUGA, FIGRS, FNGS, FSG. "We thank all who have donated to the project and to those of our partners and the many genealogical societies who spearheaded efforts to raise the funds needed, particularly the Indiana, Illinois, and Fairfax, Virginia, Genealogical Societies.".

Sources indicate that war of 1812 pensions provide information on a generation between the Revolutionary War and the 1850 census, which is the first census to provide the names of individuals in a household. The files may include an affidavit from the soldier or widow including where he enlisted, where he served, and for how long. The widow may state their date of marriage, when he died, a Bible record which may include the names and birth dates of children, and affidavits from other relatives which may help prove family relationships. Sometimes the information about the widow or an affidavit from her will disclose her maiden name. These files may also contain other meaningful military records and information on a person's fellow veterans or neighbors.

"These records are extremely valuable to researchers and historians, and we are proud to be a part of this project. We're grateful for the efforts started by the Federation of Genealogical Societies before it merged with NGS in 2020, and it has been an honor to carry this forward and continue the work with our partners to see it to completion," mentioned NGS Executive Director Matt Menashes, CAE.

"The project serves as a template for future initiatives illustrating that together, the genealogical community can help preserve and make available important genealogical records for generations to come. These records may be used not only for genealogy, but also for those studying history and as part of a school curriculum for students," stated Rencher. "Thank you to all who made this possible!".

Sources indicate that NGS offers an online course, War of 1812 Records, for anyone wanting a deeper understanding of how to interpret these records and what other records might add to the story. The modules guide participants through War of 1812 military records, historical context, and research strategies. More information and registration can be found on the NGS website.

Access the War of 1812 pension files via Fold3 and learn more about the project's completion on their blog.

SOURCE National Genealogical Society.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

by Todd Bishop on Nov 18, 2026 at 10:01 amNovember 18, 2026 at 10:08 am.

Blue Origin’s engines look like they’re off the hook, at least for now.

Industry observers note that the two BE-4 engines Blue Origin makes for United Launch Alliance’s Vulcan rocket weren’t to blame for the low thrust in Sunday’s failed launch, according to preliminary findings released Wednesday. Instead, it appears the engines didn’t get enough fuel from the rocket, ULA said.

Industry observers note that in its latest revision on the investigation, ULA said it had completed an initial integrated review of flight data. Preliminary data indicate the first stage’s low thrust came from “inadequate fuel supply from the vehicle to the BE-4 engines, not from the performance of the engines,” ULA said, adding that work remains to determine the cause.

It has been revealed that on Tuesday, ULA said early data suggested the first stage underperformed just after liftoff, leaving the rocket too low and too slow to put 40 of Amazon’s Leo internet satellites into orbit. It didn’t say then whether the engines played a role.

Sources indicate that the BE-4s are made by Jeff Bezos’ Kent, Wash.-based Blue Origin. Blue Origin CEO Dave Limp said Wednesday on X that he was proud of the BE-4 team for its “rapid response and support of ULA’s investigation” and that the company looks forward to Vulcan’s return to flight.

In a recent development, the finding matters for Blue Origin beyond Vulcan. Its own New Glenn rocket uses seven BE-4s on its first stage, and Amazon has 24 New Glenn rolls out reserved for Leo.

ULA repeated that Vulcan’s second stage appears to have started normally and that its RL10 engines operated as planned but couldn’t make up for the earlier loss of performance. The six Northrop Grumman solid rocket boosters, the source of problems on two earlier Vulcan flights, appear to have performed normally, ULA said.

The Federal Aviation Administration is overseeing the ULA-led investigation. Amazon’s next Leo launch is an Ariane 6 mission carrying 36 satellites, targeted for no earlier than Nov. 23 from French Guiana.

ULA said it will share more as the investigation continues.

📅 24 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (645 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Housingwire

⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Compass International Holdings may have filed 16 separate antitrust lawsuits against 16 separate MLS, but according to court documents filed earlier this week, those MLSs are seeking to combine these lawsuits into one.
  • In a recent development, in a motion filed on Monday to stay the lawsuit Compass filed against it, California Regional MLS (CRMLS) told the court that it and the other MLSs Compass has filed lawsuits against have asked to consolidate or coordinate the pretrial proceedings for the various Compass v.
  • According to the motion, the MLSs have also asked to include the two declaratory judgement lawsuits nine MLSs have already filed against Compass in the SDNY.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Compass International Holdings may have filed 16 separate antitrust lawsuits against 16 separate MLS, but according to court documents filed earlier this week, those MLSs are seeking to combine these lawsuits into one.

In a recent development, in a motion filed on Monday to stay the lawsuit Compass filed against it, California Regional MLS (CRMLS) told the court that it and the other MLSs Compass has filed lawsuits against have asked to consolidate or coordinate the pretrial proceedings for the various Compass v. MLS lawsuits right now pending across the country in federal court in the Southern District of New York (SDNY). If the panel declines to select New York, the motion identifies the Western District of North Carolina and the Middle District of Florida as alternative venues for the consolidated litigation.

According to the motion, the MLSs have also asked to include the two declaratory judgement lawsuits nine MLSs have already filed against Compass in the SDNY.

Sources indicate that “Compass has chosen to wage the same legal fight in courts across the country, creating unnecessary costs and the risk of conflicting rulings,” Richard Haggerty, the CEO of OneKey MLS, stated in a statement. “Each of the 16MLS organizations are challenging that approach. We believe these cases belong before one judge, and we will continue defending the cooperation rules that ensure no brokerage gains an unfair advantage by withholding publicly marketed homes from the shared marketplace.”.

This request comes after Compass informed the SDNY court that it plans to file a motion to dismiss the declaratory judgement lawsuits or to sever and transfer each MLS’s claims to the district where Compass has brought its own antitrust case against that MLS.

After months of posturing and clashes over policies, the legal dispute between Compass and the MLSs kicked off in earnest this September when Compass sent letters to MLSs across the country demanding that they stop fining agents for publicly marketing office exclusive listings. Later that month, Compass CEO Robert Reffkin told a room full of MLS executives gathered at the Council of MLSs (CMLS) that he would sue any MLS that refused to give in to Compass’s demands.

Despite Reffkin’s threats, it was actually CRMLS that made the first move, filing a lawsuit in early October seeking a declaratory judgment that its policies on listing cooperation are “fair, procompetitive, and legally sound,” according to a firm announcement. CRMLS has since been joined by Newly introduced York’s OneKey MLS in this lawsuit, while MLSListings, Arizona Regional MLS, bridgeMLS, Canopy MLS, REcolorado, Hive MLS, and Doorify MLS have filed their own lawsuit, also in the SDNY, seeking the same judgements as CRMLS and OneKey.

In the midst of these lawsuits hitting the court docket, Compass filed its own lawsuit against CRMLS, alleging that its rule unlawfully restrict how homeowners and their agents can publicly market properties outside the MLS.

In a recent development, roughly a month later, Compass reiterated those same claims in 15 separate lawsuits filed against 15 MLSs. MLS defendants in those lawsuits include bridgeMLS, Bay East MLS, Contra Costa MLS, MLSListings, The MLS-CLAW, San Diego MLS, Canopy MLS, Hive MLS, Doorify MLS, Arizona Regional MLS, Recolorado, NorthstarMLS, Houston Association of Realtors, Stellar MLS and OneKey MLS.

In an emailed statement a Compass spokesperson told HousingWire that the filing is “a procedural request  that does not change the substance of [Compass’s] claims.”.

“Each MLS applies its own rules, and the impact of those rules on agents, home sellers, and buyers is specific to its local jurisdiction,” the spokesperson added.

It remains to be seen if court will allow the MLSs to consolidate their lawsuits. This is not the first time real estate industry defendants have sought to consolidate similar lawsuits. Several real estate brokerage defendants in the copycat commission lawsuits attempted to consolidate their cases, but their request was rejected.
